It's ironic because 90% of people will read that title and think I'm being totally dramatic, but I'm sorry to disappoint you, I am not. Because I did, in fact, go from having 0 financial awareness at 21 years old to now having £135K at 26 years old. From when I was 17–21 years old, I saved my first £4,000, which I was SO proud of, but it was just sitting in a Cash ISA getting around a 3% return. At 21 years old, I began researching more about how to really “make your money work harder for you” and after watching a few YouTube videos on the topic, I ordered a book about investing. (With no real intent on getting started because honestly, I found the word scary and intimidating and didn’t think I would be clever enough to understand it) Little did I know that on 16th February 2021, when I came across a page all about compound interest and how saving £250 a month from the age of 30 could potentially end up with nearly £8M by the time I turned 60 years old, it’s safe to say, I got obsessed. It lit this fire inside me at 21 years old where I went ALL IN on saving my money and investing everything I could whilst I lived at home in my childhood bedroom. I quite literally got totally addicted to saving my money. (Definitely worse habits to have in your early 20s) 2 weeks later, on 1st March 2021, I opened up my very first Stocks & Shares ISA and honestly, the rest is history. So, you have two options. You can either keep swiping and go about your day, or you can do what I did on 1st March 2021 and take the scary leap into the world of investing because it’s safe to say it’s the best financial decision I’ve ever made. Quite simply, my future is looking pretty damn bright right about now. *When investing, your capital is at risk. Past performance is no guarantee  of future results. This information is not investment advice. Do your own research.*

Dear diary, (just kidding) there’s always this huge debate around whether we should all be selling our S&P funds and going full force into the FTSE All World, and whilst I agree there’s huge overlap, I have honestly only had great times with my S&P in the past and I really have no intention of selling mine. I haven’t contributed since the end of 2024, but I find it quite interesting just watching it grow all by itself over the years. I don’t really think there’s any point in selling it whilst it’s performing so well and, if anything, I am more interested to see how it goes over the years through its ups and downs. Also, I don’t think there’s any right and wrong between the S&P and the All World. Literally nobody knows what the future holds and there’s arguments to having both, but for now I definitely wouldn’t say the S&P is dead. And honestly, if the day ever comes when it’s on a downward decline for years on end, well… I really don’t see that day happening soon!! (Could be so wrong though lmaooo)

1. I overspend MOST months - I budget, but life isn’t black and white. Extra social plans pop up, last-minute trips happen and sometimes I just spend more than I planned to. As much as I’m a frugal gal, I also want to LIVE MY 20s. I’m not going to feel guilty about that. 2. I treat myself to a £100 gift every month - I work hard, I earn my money and I want to enjoy my income. I’m not sorry about it. 3. I buy a coffee every single day - TBF It’s £2.65 from work (it’s subsidised lol), but honestly, it’s the best £2.65 I spend at 9am every morning. I’m not willing to give it up just to save a few pounds. 4. I get my nails done every month - Believe it or not, I debate giving this up every single month. But it’s two hours where I can’t pick up my phone, I can switch off and just relax. And for me, that’s worth paying for. (and it makes me look like the put together Queen I am xx) 5. Purchasing home furnishings - I love lamps, candles, coasters, cushions, throws and all the little things that make a house feel like home. I spend a lot of time at home, and whilst I can afford it, I don’t plan on giving this up. 6. I go all out on BIG purchases - If I’m buying something expensive, best believe I’m going all out. If I’m getting a coffee machine, I want the good one. If I’m investing in something I’ll use for years, I want it to be high quality and last!! I’m still saving. I’m still investing. I’m still being sensible with my money BUT I don’t want to look back at my 20s and realise I spent the whole time trying to save as much money as possible. We can build wealth AND enjoy my life along way xx  #spendingmoney #balancedlifestyle

People have this misconception that as soon as they start investing, they'll see growth of +10%, 20%, or 30% in their first 12 months, but honestly, that couldn't be further from the truth. 9/10, your first 12 months will be so rocky that, to be honest, you're better off not even checking. The portfolios you see online with thousands didn't happen in the first 12 months. Those people have been investing for 5+ years. I can't emphasise enough that with investing, you really (really) need to be thinking about the next 10, 20, or 30 years. So here are some HONEST reminders we should probably all be reading a little more often x #investing #ISA #PersonalFinance

I know that sounds like an extremely ignorant thing to say, but I can't tell you how, why, or when, it was just something I knew growing up. I knew I wanted to start building my wealth from a young age. From the age of 16, I had this fire inside me for wealth, success, and ‘freedom’. I'd stay up until all hours watching CEOs on podcasts, studying their mindset and their character. Most of the time, they didn't even come from money themselves, which made me feel like an ‘ordinary’ girl like me could do it too. And I'm not saying this is it, the finished product. But I've built an incredible base for myself that can only accelerate from here because I'm not slowing down, and neither are my investments (so far, anyway). So if you're young like me, kind of confused about how to make moves with little to no knowledge or "impact," here are the very basics I implemented, the bricks and mortar, if you like, that paved the way for where I am today! <33
